transcript.note: Loop R1: Grid compression phase 1. Cluster vertices to eliminate empty rows/cols. Pull points from sparse regions (high col/row indices >50, empty rows >35) toward dense central area. Move southern nodes (7, 48, 14) northward, northern sparse nodes (52, 56, 57) southward. Focus on cascading removable bands.

Loop R2: Conservative grid compression. Focus on southern-east cluster (49-52, 29, 50, 51) repositioning. Pull sparse extremes (7, 11, 56) toward main body. Single-vertex moves only to avoid edge-order conflicts. Target removal of high row/col empty bands.

Loop R3: Post-compression H/V optimization. Apply diagonal-to-H/V conversions on compressed grid. Main targets: 36-44-24 col alignment, 40-12-38 col chain, 49-50-52-29-51 southern cluster alignment. Synchronized two-endpoint moves for offset-2 diagonals. Sequential cascade in main hub (23-24) and distributed clusters.

Loop R4: Ultra-conservative single-region focus. Attempt minimal H/V locks in isolated western/northern cluster (5-6-13-2) with offset-2-3 diagonals. Single-vertex moves only. Test whether compact-grid state allows any incremental improvements.

Loop R5: Convergence state. Grid compression complete (59×59 → 31×25). HV stable at 34. Attempted H/V optimizations on post-compression grid show cascading fallback violations, indicating hard constraints from edge-order and tightened layout geometry prevent further short-distance improvements. System in equilibrium.
